   149	/-- Symmetric relabeling preserves projectivity of the measurement family exactly. -/
   150	theorem relabel_isProjective_iff {X A X' A' : Type}
   151	    [Fintype X] [Fintype A] [Fintype X'] [Fintype A']
   152	    (S : SymmetricStrategy X A) (eX : X ≃ X') (eA : A ≃ A') :
   153	    (∀ x, ((relabel S eX eA).meas x).IsProjective) ↔
   154	      ∀ x, (S.meas x).IsProjective := by
   155	  constructor
   156	  · intro h x
   157	    have hx := h (eX x)
   158	    change (POVM.relabel eA (S.meas (eX.symm (eX x)))).IsProjective at hx
   159	    rw [eX.symm_apply_apply] at hx
   160	    exact (POVM.relabel_isProjective_iff eA (S.meas x)).mp hx
   161	  · intro h x
   162	    exact (POVM.relabel_isProjective_iff eA (S.meas (eX.symm x))).mpr
   163	      (h (eX.symm x))
   164	
   165	/-- Symmetric relabeling preserves consistency exactly. -/
   166	theorem relabel_isConsistent_iff {X A X' A' : Type}
   167	    [Fintype X] [Fintype A] [Fintype X'] [Fintype A']
   168	    [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq A']
   169	    (S : SymmetricStrategy X A) (eX : X ≃ X') (eA : A ≃ A') :
   170	    (relabel S eX eA).IsConsistent ↔ S.IsConsistent := by
   171	  constructor
   172	  · intro h x
   173	    have hx := h (eX x)
   174	    change (POVM.relabel eA (S.meas (eX.symm (eX x)))).IsConsistentOn S.ψ at hx
   175	    rw [eX.symm_apply_apply] at hx
   176	    exact (POVM.relabel_isConsistentOn_iff eA (S.meas x) S.ψ).mp hx
   177	  · intro h x
   178	    exact (POVM.relabel_isConsistentOn_iff eA (S.meas (eX.symm x)) S.ψ).mpr
   179	      (h (eX.symm x))
   180	
   181	/-- Symmetric relabeling preserves the SPCC predicate under the exact PMF push-forward. -/
   182	theorem relabel_isSPCC_iff {X A X' A' : Type}
   183	    [Fintype X] [Fintype A] [Fintype X'] [Fintype A']
   184	    [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq X'] [DecidableEq A']
   185	    (G : SymmetricGame X A) (G' : SymmetricGame X' A')
   186	    (S : SymmetricStrategy X A) (eX : X ≃ X') (eA : A ≃ A')
   187	    (hμ : G.μ.map (Equiv.prodCongr eX eX) = G'.μ) :
   188	    (relabel S eX eA).IsSPCC G' ↔ S.IsSPCC G := by
   189	  rw [SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC, SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC, ← hμ]
   190	  constructor
   191	  · rintro ⟨hproj, hcons, hcomm⟩
   192	    exact ⟨(relabel_isProjective_iff S eX eA).mp hproj,
   193	      (relabel_isConsistent_iff S eX eA).mp hcons,
   194	      (isCommutingOn_relabel_iff G.μ S.meas S.meas eX eX eA eA).mp hcomm⟩
   195	  · rintro ⟨hproj, hcons, hcomm⟩
   196	    exact ⟨(relabel_isProjective_iff S eX eA).mpr hproj,
   197	      (relabel_isConsistent_iff S eX eA).mpr hcons,
   198	      (isCommutingOn_relabel_iff G.μ S.meas S.meas eX eX eA eA).mpr hcomm⟩
   199	
   200	end SymmetricStrategy

   369	        (pauliQuestionEquiv P) (pauliQuestionEquiv P)
   370	        (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P) (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P)) := by
   371	      rw [pauliGame_relabel_eq]
   372	    _ = S.toStrategy.value (pauliSymmetricGame P).toGame := by
   373	      rw [pauliSymmetricGame_toGame]
   374	      change (Strategy.relabel S.toStrategy
   375	          (pauliQuestionEquiv P) (pauliQuestionEquiv P)
   376	          (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P) (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P)).value
   377	          (Game.relabel
   378	            (pauliGame (PauliParams.ofAdmissibleParams P)
   379	              (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)
   380	              (MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model))
   381	            (pauliQuestionEquiv P) (pauliQuestionEquiv P)
   382	            (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P) (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P)) =
   383	        S.toStrategy.value
   384	          (pauliGame (PauliParams.ofAdmissibleParams P)
   385	            (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)
   386	            (MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model))
   387	      exact Strategy.value_relabel
   388	        (pauliGame (PauliParams.ofAdmissibleParams P)
   389	          (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)
   390	          (MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model))
   391	        S.toStrategy (pauliQuestionEquiv P) (pauliQuestionEquiv P)
   392	        (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P) (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P)
   393	
   394	/-- Symmetric conversion preserves projectivity, consistency, and support commutation exactly. -/
   395	theorem pauliSymmetricStrategyToLibrary_isSPCC_iff
   396	    (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams)
   397	    (S : SymmetricStrategy
   398	      (PauliQuestion (PauliParams.ofAdmissibleParams P) (MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P))
   399	      (PauliAnswer (PauliParams.ofAdmissibleParams P) (MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P))) :
   400	    (pauliSymmetricStrategyToLibrary P S).IsSPCC ↔
   401	      S.IsSPCC (pauliSymmetricGame P) := by
   402	  rw [← SymmetricStrategy.isSPCC_ofSymmetricStrategy_iff
   403	    (pauliSymmetricStrategyToLibrary P S)]
   404	  change (SymmetricStrategy.relabel S (pauliQuestionEquiv P)
   405	      (pauliAnswerEquivCompact P)).IsSPCC
   406	        (SymmetricGame.ofSymmetricGame (MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliBasisTestSymm P)) ↔
   407	    S.IsSPCC (pauliSymmetricGame P)
   408	  apply SymmetricStrategy.relabel_isSPCC_iff
   409	  rw [pauliSymmetricGame_toGame]
   410	  exact pauliQuestionPMF_map P

     7	/-!
     8	# The low-degree game
     9	
    10	The low-degree component of the Pauli basis test has finite question and answer
    11	alphabets.  Its question maps act explicitly on the point, coordinate, and
    12	direction registers of the ambient coefficient space and have recursive
    13	conditionally linear representations of levels one, two, and three.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are blueprint `def:ld-game`,
    18	`def:ld-question-distribution`, and `def:ld-win-predicate`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	The exact decomposition of a scalar seed into its coordinate index and its
    21	residue records the balance assertion for the map `chi` in the same source
    22	definition.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    34	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    35	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    36	blueprint
    37	`def:ld-game`, with paper origin
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    39	-/
    40	structure LdParams where
    41	  q : ℕ
    42	  m : ℕ
    43	  d : ℕ
    44	  k : ℕ
    45	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    46	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    47	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    48	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    49	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    50	
    51	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    52	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    53	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    54	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    55	
    56	/-- The fixed scalar model of a low-degree parameter tuple.  It is a
    57	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an
    58	independently quantified field representation.  Blueprint `def:ld-game`; paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    60	-/
    61	@[reducible] noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    62	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    63	
    64	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    65	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    66	Blueprint `def:ld-game`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    68	-/
    69	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    70	
    71	/-- The three low-degree question types of blueprint
    72	`def:ld-game`, paper origin
    73	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    74	-/
    75	inductive LdType where
    76	  | point
    77	  | aline
    78	  | dline
    79	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited
    80	instance LdType.instFintype : Fintype LdType :=
    81	  ⟨{.point, .aline, .dline}, by intro x; cases x <;> simp⟩
    82	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (blueprint
    83	`def:ld-game`; paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    85	-/
    86	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    87	
    88	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (blueprint
    89	`def:ld-game`; paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    91	-/
    92	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    93	
    94	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    96	-/
    97	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    98	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    99	
   100	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
   101	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   102	-/
   103	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   104	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   105	
   106	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   107	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   108	-/
   109	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   110	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   111	
   112	/-- The zero-based coordinate index corresponding to the paper's map `χ`:
   113	`chiIndex P s` represents `χ(s) - 1` in the fixed field representation.  This
   114	is `eq:chi-func` in blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`, paper origin
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   116	-/
   117	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   118	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   119	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   120	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   121	
   122	/-! ### Formalization-only coordinate-index fibers
   123	
   124	The following decomposition supplies the equal-fiber calculation used in the
   125	uniform coordinate-index law.
   126	-/
   127	
   128	/-- The common residue set in a fiber of `chiIndex` is nonempty.  This is part
   129	of the exact seed decomposition supporting the balance assertion in
   130	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `lem:chi-seed-fibers`, paper
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:215-221`.
   132	-/
   133	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   134	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   135	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   136	    rw [hq]
   137	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm
   138	
   139	/-- Divisibility identifies the scalar cardinality with the product of the
   140	coordinate-index cardinality and the common fiber cardinality.  This supports
   141	`lem:chi-seed-fibers` in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   142	theorem LdParams.seedFiberProduct_eq (L : LdParams) :
   143	    L.q = L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   144	  (Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd).symm
   145	
   146	/-- Casting between equal finite cardinalities preserves the underlying
   147	natural-number representative. -/
   148	@[simp] private theorem equivCastFin_val {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (i : Fin m) :
   149	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin h) i).val = i.val := by
   150	  subst n
   151	  rfl
   152	
   153	/-- A scalar seed is uniquely a coordinate index and a residue in its
   154	`chiIndex` fiber.  This is the exact decomposition underlying
   155	`lem:chi-seed-fibers` in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   156	noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   157	    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
   158	  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|
   159	    (Equiv.cast <| congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq).trans
   160	      finProdFinEquiv.symm
   161	
   162	/-- The coordinate component of the exact seed decomposition is `chiIndex`. -/
   163	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
   164	    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
   165	  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩
   166	  have hquot : (binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   167	    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
   168	    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
   169	    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
   170	  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
   171	  apply Fin.ext
   172	  change
   173	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
   174	      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
   175	      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val
   176	  rw [equivCastFin_val]
   177	  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
   178	  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq
   179	
   180	/-- Reconstruct the scalar seed belonging to a coordinate and its fiber
   181	residue. -/
   182	noncomputable def seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   183	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ScalarQ L :=
   184	  (seedFiberEquiv L).symm (i, r)
   185	
   186	/-- Decomposing a reconstructed seed recovers its coordinate and residue. -/
   187	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   188	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   189	    seedFiberEquiv L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = (i, r) :=
   190	  (seedFiberEquiv L).apply_symm_apply (i, r)
   191	
   192	/-- A reconstructed seed belongs to the prescribed `chiIndex` fiber. -/
   193	@[simp] theorem chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   194	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   195	    chiIndex L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = i := by
   196	  rw [← seedFiberEquiv_fst]
   197	  simp
   198	
   199	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   200	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   201	prefix restriction in blueprint
   202	`def:ld-question-distribution`, paper origin
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   204	-/
   205	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   206	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   207	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   208	
   209	/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding a fixed index is idempotent.  This is a
   210	formalization-only consequence of the prefix restriction in
   211	`def:ld-question-distribution`, recorded as `lem:prefix-projection-idempotent`
   212	in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   213	theorem prefixProjection_idempotent {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m)
   214	    (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   215	    prefixProjection i (prefixProjection i v) = prefixProjection i v := by
   216	  funext j
   217	  by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   218	  · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h]
   219	  · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   220	
   221	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   222	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of blueprint
   223	`def:ld-question-distribution`, paper origin
   224	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   225	-/
   226	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   227	  fun i => match i with
   228	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   229	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   230	  | .inr _ => 0
   231	
   232	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   233	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   234	is retained (blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`; paper
   235	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   236	-/
   237	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   238	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   239	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   240	  fun i => match i with
   241	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   242	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   243	  | .inr _ => 0
   244	
   245	/-- The diagonal-line CL map applies the canonical line representative map to
   246	the point block and stores the prefix-projected direction in the direction
   247	block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   248	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   249	`def:ld-question-distribution`; paper origin
   250	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   251	-/
   252	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   253	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   254	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   255	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   256	  fun i => match i with
   257	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   258	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   259	  | .inr j => direction j
   260	
   261	/-- The conditionally linear map attached to each low-degree question type.
   262	This is the typed construction in blueprint
   263	`def:ld-question-distribution`, paper origin
   264	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   265	-/
   266	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   267	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   268	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   269	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   270	
   271	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   272	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   273	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   274	blueprint
   275	`def:ld-question-distribution`, paper origin
   276	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   277	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   278	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}
   279	
   280	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   281	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   282	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   283	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P)
   284	
   285	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the direction
   286	coordinates of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   287	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   288	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P)
   289	
   290	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   291	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   292	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   293	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   294	  toFun x := fun i =>
   295	    match i with
   296	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   297	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   298	    | .inr _ => 0
   299	  map_add' x y := by
   300	    funext i
   301	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   302	  map_smul' c x := by
   303	    funext i
   304	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   305	
   306	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   307	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   308	other coordinate. -/
   309	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   310	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   311	  toFun x := fun i =>
   312	    match i with
   313	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   314	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   315	    | .inr _ => 0
   316	  map_add' x y := by
   317	    funext i
   318	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   319	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   320	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   321	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   322	      rfl
   323	    · simp
   324	    · simp
   325	  map_smul' c x := by
   326	    funext i
   327	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   328	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   329	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   330	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   331	      rfl
   332	    · simp
   333	    · simp
   334	
   335	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   336	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   337	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   338	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   339	  toFun x := fun k =>
   340	    match k with
   341	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   342	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   343	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   344	  map_add' x y := by
   345	    funext k
   346	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   347	    · simp
   348	    · simp
   349	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   350	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   351	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   352	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   353	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   354	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   355	        rfl
   356	  map_smul' c x := by
   357	    funext k
   358	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   359	    · simp
   360	    · simp
   361	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   362	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   363	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   364	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   365	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   366	        rfl
   367	
   368	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the shared-scalar map vanishes
   369	outside the scalar register. -/
   370	private theorem ldSeedLinear_supported (P : LdParams) :
   371	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldSeedRegister P →
   372	      ldSeedLinear P x i = 0 := by
   373	  intro x i hi
   374	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   375	  · rfl
   376	  · cases u
   377	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_singleton_self _) hi
   378	  · rfl
   379	
   380	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the canonical-representative map
   381	vanishes outside the point register. -/
   382	private theorem ldPointCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   383	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldPointRegister P →
   384	      ldPointCLLinear P v x i = 0 := by
   385	  intro x i hi
   386	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   387	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hi
   388	  · rfl
   389	  · rfl
   390	
   391	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the prefix-zeroing map vanishes
   392	outside the direction register. -/
   393	private theorem ldDirectionCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   394	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (k : LdIndex P), k ∉ ldDirectionRegister P →
   395	      ldDirectionCLLinear P i x k = 0 := by
   396	  intro x k hk
   397	  rcases k with (j | u) | j
   398	  · rfl
   399	  · rfl
   400	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hk
   401	
   402	/-- Formalization-only disjointness lemma for the conditional-linearity
   403	decomposition: the image of any coordinate embedding that avoids the scalar
   404	coordinate lies in the complement of the scalar register.  This supports
   405	`def:ld-question-distribution` in
   406	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   407	theorem ldCoordinateRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams)
   408	    (e : Fin P.m → LdIndex P) (he : ∀ j, e j ≠ Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) :
   409	    Finset.univ.image e ⊆ Finset.univ \ {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())} := by
   410	  intro i hi
   411	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   412	  simp [he j]

   415	both the scalar and the direction registers. -/
   416	private theorem ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction (P : LdParams) :
   417	    ldPointRegister P ⊆
   418	      (Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P) \ ldDirectionRegister P := by

   420	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   421	  simp [ldSeedRegister, ldDirectionRegister]

   423	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the scalar register

   426	    coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) =

   428	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldSeedRegister P :=

   430	  simp [coordinateRestriction, hmem]

   435	    LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) = LdSpace.point x := by

   444	    LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) =

     7	/-!
     8	# The Pauli basis test
     9	
    10	This file supplies the finite question and answer alphabets, the typed
    11	conditionally-linear question sampler, and the Boolean win predicate for the
    12	Pauli basis test.  The quantitative soundness theorem is isolated in
    13	`Soundness.lean`.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are blueprint `def:admissible`,
    18	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, and `def:pauli-win-predicate`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-1225`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT

    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter tuple.  Its scalar carrier
    31	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    32	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    33	is blueprint
    34	`def:admissible`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    36	-/
    37	structure AdmissibleParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	
    45	/-- Every admissible parameter tuple has positive ambient dimension. This
    46	follows from positivity of the admissible field size and the divisibility
    47	`P.m ∣ P.q` in `def:admissible`, blueprint
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    50	-/
    51	theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
    52	  have hqpos : 0 < P.q := by
    53	    rcases P.hq with ⟨k, _, hq⟩
    54	    rw [hq]
    55	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)
    56	  exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr
    57	    (ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt hqpos) P.hdvd)
    58	
    59	/-- The fixed scalar model of an admissible parameter tuple.  It is a
    60	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
    61	quantified field representation.  This is the field representation of
    62	`def:admissible`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`; paper
    63	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    64	-/
    65	@[reducible] noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model
    66	    (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    67	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    68	
    69	/-- The low-degree parameter tuple determined by an admissible Pauli-test
    70	tuple.  It is not an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  The low-degree
    71	parameters are those of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    72	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
    73	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    74	-/
    75	@[reducible] def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
    76	  q := P.q
    77	  m := P.m
    78	  d := P.d
    79	  k := 1
    80	  hm := P.one_le_m
    81	  hd := P.hd
    82	  hk := by decide
    83	  hq := P.hq
    84	  hdvd := P.hdvd

    86	/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter tuple.  It is
    87	the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
    88	blueprint
    89	`def:admissible`, paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.

    93	
    94	/-- The six families of Pauli-test questions.  This is part of
    95	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
    96	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.

    98	inductive PauliType where
    99	  | point (W : PauliKind)
   100	  | aline (W : PauliKind)
   101	  | dline (W : PauliKind)
   102	  | pauli (W : PauliKind)
   103	  | pairW (W : PauliKind)
   104	  | pair
   105	  | ms (t : MsType)
   106	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

   108	/-- The register blocks used by the Pauli question space.  These are the
   109	coordinates displayed in blueprint
   110	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   112	-/
   113	abbrev PauliIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   114	  (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)
   115	
   116	/-- The ambient Pauli question coefficient space (blueprint
   117	`def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper origin
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   119	-/
   120	abbrev PauliSpace (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliIndex P → PauliScalar P
   121	
   122	/-- The coefficient register indexed by the Boolean cube in
   123	blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
   124	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-945`.
   125	-/
   126	abbrev PauliRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) := Cube P.m → PauliScalar P
   127	
   128	/- The nested sum is the fixed register order
   129	`V_X ⊕ V_Z ⊕ V_I ⊕ V_V ⊕ V_{R_X} ⊕ V_{R_Z}` from the blueprint. -/
   130	/-- The `V_X` block of an ambient Pauli vector (blueprint
   131	`def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`). -/
   133	def pauliXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   134	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl i)))))
   135	
   136	/-- The `V_Z` block of an ambient Pauli vector in blueprint
   137	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
   138	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   139	-/
   140	def pauliZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   141	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))))
   142	
   143	/-- The scalar block `V_I` of an ambient Pauli vector in
   144	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   145	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   146	-/
   147	def pauliScalarBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   148	  z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr ()))))
   149	
   150	/-- The direction block `V_V` of an ambient Pauli vector in
   151	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   152	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   153	-/
   154	def pauliDirectionBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   155	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))
   156	
   157	/-- The `r_X` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
   158	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   159	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   160	-/
   161	def pauliRXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   162	  z (.inl (.inr ()))
   163	
   164	/-- The `r_Z` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
   165	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   166	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   167	-/
   168	def pauliRZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   169	  z (.inr ())
   170	
   171	/-- Select the basis-dependent point block from a Pauli question content in
   172	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   173	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   174	-/
   175	def pauliPointBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   176	    Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   177	  match W with
   178	  | .X => pauliXBlock z
   179	  | .Z => pauliZBlock z
   180	
   181	/-- Read the low-degree register selected by a basis from an ambient Pauli
   182	vector.  This is restriction to the basis-selected registers of
   183	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
   184	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   185	-/
   186	def pauliToLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   187	    LdSpace P.toLdParams :=
   188	  fun i => match i with
   189	  | .inl (.inl j) => pauliPointBlock W z j
   190	  | .inl (.inr _) => pauliScalarBlock z
   191	  | .inr j => pauliDirectionBlock z j
   192	
   193	/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
   194	other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is extension into the
   195	basis-selected registers of `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   196	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
   197	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   198	-/
   199	def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   200	    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
   201	  fun i => match i with
   202	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   203	      match W with
   204	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   205	      | .Z => 0
   206	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   207	      match W with
   208	      | .X => 0
   209	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   210	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   211	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   212	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   213	  | .inr _ => 0
   214	
   215	/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from
   216	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
   217	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   218	-/
   219	def pauliSharedProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliSpace P :=
   220	  fun i => match i with
   221	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))))
   222	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
   223	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   224	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   225	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   226	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

   228	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   229	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   230	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   231	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   232	`def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper origin
   233	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   234	-/
   235	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   236	  | .point _ => 1
   237	  | .aline _ => 2
   238	  | .dline _ => 3
   239	  | .pauli _ => 0
   240	  | .pairW _ => 1
   241	  | .pair => 1
   242	  | .ms _ => 1
   243	
   244	/-- The conditionally linear map attached to each Pauli question type.  The
   245	point and line maps are the corresponding
   246	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   247	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   248	is the direct finite-space form of blueprint
   249	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
   250	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   251	-/
   252	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   253	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   254	  match t with
   255	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   256	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   257	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   258	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   259	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   260	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   261	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection
   262	
   263	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the type-4 projection of the ambient Pauli
   264	coefficient space, presented as a linear map; see `pauliSharedProjection` and
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`,
   266	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
   267	private def pauliSharedProjectionLinear (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   268	    PauliSpace P →ₗ[PauliScalar P] PauliSpace P where
   269	  toFun z := pauliSharedProjection z
   270	  map_add' x y := by
   271	    funext i
   272	    rcases i with ((((j | j) | u) | j) | u) | u <;> simp [pauliSharedProjection]
   273	  map_smul' c x := by
   274	    funext i
   275	    rcases i with ((((j | j) | u) | j) | u) | u <;> simp [pauliSharedProjection]
   276	
   277	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the inclusion of the low-degree register index
   278	into the ambient Pauli register index selected by a basis.  It realizes the
   279	natural embedding of the range of the low-degree maps described in
   280	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`,
   281	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
   282	private def pauliLdIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) :
   283	    LdIndex P.toLdParams → PauliIndex P
   284	  | .inl (.inl j) =>
   285	      match W with
   286	      | .X => .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j))))
   287	      | .Z => .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j))))
   288	  | .inl (.inr _) => .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr ())))
   289	  | .inr j => .inl (.inl (.inr j))
   290	
   291	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: distinct low-degree registers are sent to
   292	distinct ambient Pauli registers; see `pauliLdIndex`. -/
   293	private theorem pauliLdIndex_injective (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) :
   294	    Function.Injective (pauliLdIndex P W) := by
   295	  intro a b hab
   296	  cases W <;> rcases a with (j | u) | j <;> rcases b with (j' | u') | j' <;>
   297	    simp_all [pauliLdIndex] <;> injection hab
   298	
   299	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: reading the low-degree register out of an
   300	ambient Pauli vector is restriction along `pauliLdIndex`; see
   301	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`,
   302	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
   303	private theorem pauliToLd_eq (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   304	    (z : PauliSpace P) :
   305	    pauliToLd P W z = fun k => z (pauliLdIndex P W k) := by
   306	  funext k
   307	  rcases k with (j | u) | j <;> cases W <;> rfl
   308	
   309	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: writing a low-degree vector into the ambient
   310	Pauli registers is extension by zero along `pauliLdIndex`; see
   311	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`,
   312	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
   313	private theorem embedLd_eq (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   314	    (w : LdSpace P.toLdParams) :
   315	    embedLd P W w = Function.extend (pauliLdIndex P W) w 0 := by
   316	  have hf := pauliLdIndex_injective P W
   317	  have hz : ∀ i : PauliIndex P, (∀ k, pauliLdIndex P W k ≠ i) →
   318	      Function.extend (pauliLdIndex P W) w (0 : PauliSpace P) i = 0 :=
   319	    fun i hi => Function.extend_apply' w (0 : PauliSpace P) i
   320	      (fun hex => hi hex.choose hex.choose_spec)
   321	  funext i
   322	  rcases i with ((((j | j) | u) | j) | u) | u
   323	  · cases W
   324	    · exact (hf.extend_apply w 0 (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j))).symm
   325	    · exact (hz _ (by rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   326	  · cases W
   327	    · exact (hz _ (by rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   328	    · exact (hf.extend_apply w 0 (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j))).symm
   329	  · exact (hf.extend_apply w 0 (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))).symm
   330	  · exact (hf.extend_apply w 0 (Sum.inr j)).symm
   331	  · exact (hz _ (by
   332	      intro k
   333	      cases W <;> rcases k with (j' | u') | j' <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   334	  · exact (hz _ (by
   335	      intro k
   336	      cases W <;> rcases k with (j' | u') | j' <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   337	
   338	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the typed Pauli point, axis-line, and
   339	diagonal-line maps are the corresponding low-degree maps reindexed along
   340	`pauliLdIndex`.  This is items 1--3 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   341	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`,
   342	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
   343	private theorem pauliCL_reindex (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   344	    (L : LdSpace P.toLdParams → LdSpace P.toLdParams) :
   345	    (fun z : PauliSpace P => embedLd P W (L (pauliToLd P W z))) =
   346	      fun z => Function.extend (pauliLdIndex P W)
   347	        (L (fun k => z (pauliLdIndex P W k))) 0 := by
   348	  funext z
   349	  rw [embedLd_eq, pauliToLd_eq]
   350	
   351	/-- Every Pauli question map is conditionally linear at its specified level:
   352	point maps have level one, axis-line maps level two, diagonal-line maps level
   353	three, Pauli maps level zero, and all pair and Magic Square maps level one.
   354	This is `lem:pauli-question-cl-components` in
   355	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, with paper origin
   356	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   357	The assertion concerns the individual levels and does not choose one common
   358	level for the whole family. -/
   359	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   360	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   361	  have hshared : IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 1
   362	      (pauliSharedProjection (P := P)) :=
   363	    isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear (pauliSharedProjectionLinear P)
   364	  cases t with
   365	  | point W =>
   366	      show IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 1
   367	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>
   368	          embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z)))
   369	      rw [pauliCL_reindex P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams)]
   370	      exact isCondLinearOn_reindex (pauliLdIndex_injective P W)
   371	        (isCondLinear_ldPointCL P.toLdParams)
   372	  | aline W =>
   373	      show IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 2
   374	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>
   375	          embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z)))
   376	      rw [pauliCL_reindex P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams)]
   377	      exact isCondLinearOn_reindex (pauliLdIndex_injective P W)
   378	        (isCondLinear_ldALineCL P.toLdParams)
   379	  | dline W =>
   380	      show IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 3
   381	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>
   382	          embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z)))
   383	      rw [pauliCL_reindex P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams)]
   384	      exact isCondLinearOn_reindex (pauliLdIndex_injective P W)
   385	        (isCondLinear_ldDLineCL P.toLdParams)
   386	  | pauli W => exact ⟨.zero, trivial, rfl⟩
   387	  | pairW W => exact hshared
   388	  | pair => exact hshared
   389	  | ms s => exact hshared
   390	
   391	/-- The Pauli question maps form a typed family of three-level conditionally
   392	linear functions after each component is raised from its specified level. This
   393	is `lem:pauli-question-cl-family` in
   394	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, with paper origin
   395	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1084-1120`.
   396	-/
   397	theorem isTypedCondLinearFamily_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   398	    IsTypedCondLinearFamily (PauliScalar P) PauliType 3 (pauliCL P) := by
   399	  intro t
   400	  exact IsCondLinearOn.mono_level (isCondLinear_pauliCL P t) (by
   401	    cases t <;> simp [pauliCLLevel])
   402	
   403	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   404	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   405	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
   406	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   407	-/
   408	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   409	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   410	  let lineEdges :=
   411	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   412	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   413	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   414	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   415	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   416	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   417	  let basisEdges :=
   418	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   419	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   420	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   421	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   422	  let pairEdges :=
   423	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   424	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   425	  let msEdges' :=
   426	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   427	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   428	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   429	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   430	
   431	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   432	(blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper
   433	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   434	-/
   435	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   436	
   437	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   438	blueprint `def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   440	Its ambient coefficient vector is zero. -/
   441	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   442	  (.pauli W, 0)
   443	
   444	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   445	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`, used to state
   446	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   447	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
   448	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   449	-/
   450	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   451	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   452	
   453	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   454	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   455	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   456	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   457	-/
   458	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   459	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   460	  simp [pauliEdges]
   461	
   462	set_option maxRecDepth 10000 in
   463	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
   464	-- Deciding the cardinality unfolds the nested finite sum and product alphabets.
   465	/-- The ordered carrier of the Pauli question graph has `86` edges: its
   466	`26` loops occur once, while its `30` non-loop undirected edges occur in both
   467	orientations. This finite computation supports the explicit quantitative
   468	baseline for `thm:pauli`; the graph itself is unchanged. -/
   469	theorem pauli_edge_card : Fintype.card PauliEdge = 86 := by
   470	  decide
   471	
   472	/-- The Pauli question distribution from blueprint
   473	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
   474	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   475	-/
   476	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   477	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   478	  by
   479	    classical
   480	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   481	    exact
   482	      Distribution.map
   483	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   484	        (fun s =>
   485	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   486	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   487	
   488	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   489	the seven answer forms in blueprint `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   490	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   491	-/
   492	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   493	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   494	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   495	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   496	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   497	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   498	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   499	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   500	  deriving DecidableEq
   501	
   502	/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Pauli-test answer
   503	alphabet to a Pauli register. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a
   504	Pauli question yields a complete `PauliRegister`-indexed measurement. -/
   505	def pauliAnswerOrZero {P : AdmissibleParams} : PauliAnswer P → PauliRegister P
   506	  | .pauliOutcome u => u
   507	  | _ => 0
   508	
   509	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   510	answer alphabet in blueprint
   511	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
   512	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   513	-/
   514	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   515	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   516	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   517	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   518	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   519	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   520

item.text: The game bridges establish exact equality with the already reviewed library games, including all 86 ordered Pauli edges and every verifier constructor case. One explicit proof uses the repository’s warning threshold (`4,000,000` heartbeats and recursion depth `10,000`); I’m checking whether that is justified by unavoidable finite case analysis or masks an unstable proof before deciding whether it merits an advisory.

     8	/-!
     9	# Low-degree sampling and polynomial measurements
    10	
    11	The low-degree question laws have uniform point and coordinate-index marginals,
    12	and every sampled line is incident to its paired point.  Polynomial outcomes
    13	are bounded multivariate polynomials. The soundness theorem using these
    14	definitions is proved in `LowDegreeGameTheorems`.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The principal definition and theorem are blueprint `def:ld-meas` and
    19	`lem:ld-soundness`. Their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-287,392-480`.
    21	The dimension-divisibility hypothesis is documented in
    22	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    23	-/

    39	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
    40	vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
    41	def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    42	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    43	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    44	  invFun p := fun i =>
    45	    match i with
    46	    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
    47	    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
    48	    | .inr j => p.2 j
    49	  left_inv z := by
    50	    funext i
    51	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
    52	    · rfl
    53	    · cases u
    54	      rfl
    55	    · rfl
    56	  right_inv p := by
    57	    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
    58	    rfl

    62	private theorem map_uniformDistribution_point (L : LdParams) :
    63	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
    64	      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
    65	  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
    66	      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
    67	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
    68	  calc
    69	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
    70	        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
    71	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
    72	          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    73	          rfl
    74	    _ = ((uniformDistribution
    75	          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
    76	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
    77	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
    78	          rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]

   260	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (L : LdParams) :

   271	      simp
   272	    change Distribution.uniformOnFinset _ = _
   273	    rw [hfilter]
   274	    rfl
   275	  have hleft : ldQuestionDistribution L =
   276	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))

   279	    rw [bind_uniformDistribution_map]

   285	            fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by

   287	    have hfamily : (fun uv : LdType × LdType =>
   288	        (clDistribution (ldCL L uv.1) (ldCL L uv.2)).map

   291	        fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z)) := by
   292	      funext uv
   293	      exact Distribution.map_map _ _ _
   294	    change Distribution.bind (graphDistribution _ hE) _ = _
   295	    rw [hgraph hE, hfamily]
   296	  rw [hleft, hright]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check that each checked-in comparator challenge is freshly regenerated.

Every configuration under ``challenges/`` describes one challenge.  A challenge
whose expected file exists is regenerated in a temporary directory and byte
compared; a challenge whose expected file does not exist yet is skipped with a
message, unless its configuration sets ``require_expected``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import difflib
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from challenge_config import (
    ChallengeConfig,
    ChallengeConfigError,
    load_challenges,
)
from assemble_challenge import assemble, assemble_split

# These belong to the scripts, not to the tree under `--root`: the checked tree
# may be a different worktree than the one this script was invoked from.
SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
EXTRACTOR = SCRIPT_DIR / "extract_closure.lean"
ASSEMBLER = SCRIPT_DIR / "assemble_challenge.py"

# A Lean module header cannot be computed at elaboration time, so the extractor
# is rendered per challenge with its own import block substituted.
IMPORT_BLOCK = re.compile(r"\A(?:[ \t]*\n)*(?:import[ \t]+\S+[^\n]*\n)+")


def run(
    cmd: Sequence[str],
    *,
    cwd: Path,
    stdout: Path | None = None,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> str:
    if stdout is None:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            cwd=cwd,
            check=True,
            text=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            env=env,
        )
        return completed.stdout

    with stdout.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, check=True, text=True, stdout=handle, env=env)
    return ""


def clean_closure_rows(raw_tsv: Path, clean_tsv: Path) -> None:
    rows = []
    for line in raw_tsv.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if len(line.split("\t")) in (4, 5):
            rows.append(line)
    clean_tsv.write_text("\n".join(rows) + ("\n" if rows else ""), encoding="utf-8")


def read_expected_tree(expected_dir: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    if not expected_dir.is_dir():
        return {}
    return {
        str(path.relative_to(expected_dir)): path.read_bytes()
        for path in sorted(expected_dir.rglob("*.lean"))
    }


def tree_diff(expected: dict[str, bytes], candidate: dict[str, bytes]) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []
    for rel in sorted(set(expected) | set(candidate)):
        old_bytes = expected.get(rel)
        new_bytes = candidate.get(rel)
        if old_bytes == new_bytes:
            continue
        if old_bytes is None:
            out.append(f"--- missing from the checked-in copy: {rel}\n")
            continue
        if new_bytes is None:
            out.append(f"--- no longer generated: {rel}\n")
            continue
        out.extend(
            difflib.unified_diff(
                old_bytes.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines(True),
                new_bytes.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines(True),
                fromfile=f"checked-in {rel}",
                tofile=f"regenerated {rel}",
            )
        )
    return "".join(out)


def render_extractor(challenge: ChallengeConfig, template: str) -> str:
    """The extractor source with this challenge's import block substituted."""
    body, substitutions = IMPORT_BLOCK.subn(
        lambda _: challenge.import_block(), template, count=1
    )
    if substitutions != 1:
        raise ChallengeConfigError(
            f"{EXTRACTOR} does not start with an import block; cannot render "
            f"challenge {challenge.name!r}"
        )
    return body


def challenge_part(root: Path, relative: str | None) -> bytes:
    """A header or footer file's bytes; empty when unconfigured or absent.

    A challenge under development is generated before its footer exists;
    `missing_challenge_inputs` reports what was left out.  Only `--write`
    generates such a challenge: `check_challenge` refuses to `--update` it, so
    a checked-in expected copy is never written with a part left out.
    """
    if relative is None:
        return b""
    path = root / relative
    return path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else b""


def closure_tsv(root: Path, workdir: Path, challenge: ChallengeConfig) -> Path:
    """Run the rendered extractor and return its cleaned closure TSV."""
    raw_tsv = workdir / "closure.tsv"
    clean_tsv = workdir / "closure.clean.tsv"
    extractor = workdir / "extract_closure.lean"
    extractor.write_text(
        render_extractor(challenge, EXTRACTOR.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(challenge.extractor_env())
    run(["lake", "env", "lean", str(extractor)], cwd=root, stdout=raw_tsv, env=env)
    clean_closure_rows(raw_tsv, clean_tsv)
    return clean_tsv


def assemble_candidate(root: Path, workdir: Path, challenge: ChallengeConfig) -> Path:
    body = workdir / "draft.lean"
    candidate = workdir / "Challenge.lean"
    body.write_text(
        assemble(challenge, root, closure_tsv(root, workdir, challenge)),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    candidate.write_bytes(
        challenge_part(root, challenge.header)
        + body.read_bytes()
        + b"\n"
        + challenge_part(root, challenge.footer)
    )
    return candidate


def assemble_split_candidate(
    root: Path, workdir: Path, challenge: ChallengeConfig
) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    files = assemble_split(challenge, root, closure_tsv(root, workdir, challenge))
    return {rel: text.encode("utf-8") for rel, text in files.items()}


def write_tree(destination: Path, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
    if destination.exists():
        if destination.is_dir():
            shutil.rmtree(destination)
        else:
            destination.unlink()
    for relative, data in files.items():
        path = destination / relative
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(data)


def unified_diff(expected: Path, candidate: Path) -> str:
    expected_text = expected.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(True)
    candidate_text = candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(True)
    return "".join(
        difflib.unified_diff(
            expected_text,
            candidate_text,
            fromfile=str(expected),
            tofile="regenerated Challenge.lean",
        )
    )


def missing_challenge_inputs(root: Path, challenge: ChallengeConfig) -> list[str]:
    """Header/footer files the configuration names but the tree does not have."""
    return [
        part
        for part in (challenge.header, challenge.footer)
        if part is not None and not (root / part).exists()

) -> int:
    expected = root / challenge.expected

    if not (update or write) and not expected.exists():
        if challenge.require_expected:
            print(
                f"::error::challenge {challenge.name!r}: {challenge.expected} does "
                "not exist; run `python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py "
                f"--root . --challenge {challenge.name} --update`",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 1
        print(
            f"challenge {challenge.name!r}: no expected file yet "
            f"({challenge.expected}); skipping the drift check"
        )
        return 0

    absent = missing_challenge_inputs(root, challenge)

def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=Path.cwd(),
        help="repository root (default: current directory)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--challenge",
        action="append",
        metavar="NAME",
        help=(
            "challenge name under challenges/, or a path to a configuration "
            "file; repeatable (default: every configured challenge)"
        ),
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--update",
        action="store_true",
        help="rewrite the checked-in generated challenge copy",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--write",
        type=Path,
        metavar="PATH",
        help="write the regenerated challenge to PATH instead of comparing; "
        "requires exactly one --challenge and leaves the expected copy alone",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        challenges = load_challenges(args.challenge)
    except ChallengeConfigError as exc:
        print(f"::error::{exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if args.write is not None and len(challenges) != 1:
        print(
            "::error::--write needs exactly one --challenge",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    if not challenges:
        print("::error::no challenge configuration found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    root = args.root.resolve()
    status = 0
    for challenge in challenges:
        status |= check_challenge(
            root, challenge, update=args.update, write=args.write
        )
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Regression tests for multi-challenge comparator configuration."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io

from contextlib import redirect_stderr, redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
COMPARATOR = REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "comparator"

# The comparator scripts import each other by module name, the way Python puts
# a script's own directory on the path; importing them here the same way keeps
# one `challenge_config` module object, so exception classes compare equal.
if str(COMPARATOR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(COMPARATOR))

import assemble_challenge  # noqa: E402

MINIMAL = {
    "name": "sample",
    "imports": ["MIPStarRE.Foo"],
    "targets": ["MIPStarRE.Foo.bar"],
    "expected": "scripts/comparator/expected/sample.expected",
}


def write_config(directory: Path, name: str, **overrides) -> Path:
    data = dict(MINIMAL, name=name)
    data.update(overrides)
    path = directory / f"{name}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
    return path

class MultiTargetAssemblyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The assembler orders a many-module closure by import rank, then line."""

    def _tree(self, root: Path) -> None:
        (root / "MIPStarRE").mkdir(parents=True)
        (root / "MIPStarRE" / "Base.lean").write_text(
            "\n".join(
                [
                    "import Mathlib",
                    "namespace MIPStarRE",
                    "def base : Nat := 0",
                    "def later : Nat := 1",
                    "end MIPStarRE",
                ]
            )
            + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        (root / "MIPStarRE" / "Mid.lean").write_text(
            "\n".join(
                [
                    "import MIPStarRE.Base",
                    "namespace MIPStarRE",
                    "def mid : Nat := base",
                    "end MIPStarRE",
                ]
            )
            + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        (root / "MIPStarRE" / "Top.lean").write_text(
            "\n".join(
                [
                    "import MIPStarRE.Mid",
                    "namespace MIPStarRE",
                    "def top : Nat := mid",
                    "end MIPStarRE",
                ]
            )
            + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )

    def _tsv(self, root: Path) -> Path:
        # deliberately shuffled, and mixing the two targets' closures
        tsv = root / "closure.clean.tsv"
        tsv.write_text(
            "\n".join(
                [
                    "MIPStarRE.top\tMIPStarRE/Top.lean\t3\t3",
                    "MIPStarRE.later\tMIPStarRE/Base.lean\t4\t4",
                    "MIPStarRE.mid\tMIPStarRE/Mid.lean\t3\t3",
                    "MIPStarRE.base\tMIPStarRE/Base.lean\t3\t3",
                    "MIPStarRE.generated\tMIPStarRE/Top.lean\tNORANGE\tNORANGE",
                ]
            )
            + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        return tsv

    def test_declarations_follow_import_rank_then_line_number(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            root = Path(td)
            self._tree(root)
            tsv = self._tsv(root)
            challenge = challenge_config.load_challenge(
                write_config(root, "sample", targets=["MIPStarRE.top", "MIPStarRE.later"])
            )

            body = assemble_challenge.assemble(challenge, root, tsv)

            order = [
                line.split("(")[1].rstrip(")")
                for line in body.splitlines()
                if line.startswith("-- source:")
            ]
            self.assertEqual(
                order,
                ["MIPStarRE.base", "MIPStarRE.later", "MIPStarRE.mid", "MIPStarRE.top"],
            )
            self.assertIn("--   MIPStarRE.generated  (from MIPStarRE/Top.lean)", body)

    def test_assembly_is_independent_of_the_row_order(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            root = Path(td)
            self._tree(root)
            tsv = self._tsv(root)
            challenge = challenge_config.load_challenge(write_config(root, "sample"))
            first = assemble_challenge.assemble(challenge, root, tsv)

            rows = tsv.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
            tsv.write_text("\n".join(reversed(rows)) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            second = assemble_challenge.assemble(challenge, root, tsv)

        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_provenance_comments_can_be_disabled(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            root = Path(td)
            self._tree(root)
            tsv = self._tsv(root)
            challenge = challenge_config.load_challenge(
                write_config(root, "sample", provenance_comments=False)
            )

            body = assemble_challenge.assemble(challenge, root, tsv)

        self.assertNotIn("-- source:", body)
        self.assertLess(body.index("def base"), body.index("def later"))
        self.assertLess(body.index("def later"), body.index("def mid"))
        self.assertLess(body.index("def mid"), body.index("def top"))
        self.assertIn("--   MIPStarRE.generated  (from MIPStarRE/Top.lean)", body)

    def test_stale_context_table_names_the_offending_challenge(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            root = Path(td)
            self._tree(root)
            tsv = self._tsv(root)
            challenge = challenge_config.load_challenge(
                write_config(root, "sample", extras={"MIPStarRE.gone": ["-- x"]})
            )

            with self.assertRaises(assemble_challenge.StaleContextTables) as ctx:
                assemble_challenge.assemble(challenge, root, tsv)

            message = str(ctx.exception)
            self.assertIn("sample.json", message)
            self.assertIn("MIPStarRE.gone", message)

class DefinitionFrontierExtractionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    FIXTURE = """
namespace MIPStarRE.ComparatorDefinitionFrontierFixture

def typeDependency : Type := Nat
def registeredValueHelper : Nat := 7
def registered (_n : typeDependency) : Nat := registeredValueHelper
theorem ordinaryProofHelper (n : Nat) : n = n := rfl
def ordinaryValueHelper : Nat := 1
def ordinary : { n : Nat // n = n } :=
  ⟨registered ordinaryValueHelper, ordinaryProofHelper _⟩
theorem target : ordinary = ordinary := rfl

end MIPStarRE.ComparatorDefinitionFrontierFixture
"""

    def _run_extractor(self, definition_names: str | None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        template = (COMPARATOR / "extract_closure.lean").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        source = check_challenge_drift.IMPORT_BLOCK.sub(
            "import Mathlib\n", template, count=1
        )
        source = source.replace(
            "\n#eval runExtract\n",
            "\n" + textwrap.dedent(self.FIXTURE) + "\n#eval runExtract\n",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            extractor = Path(td) / "extract_fixture.lean"
            extractor.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
            env = dict(os.environ)
            env[challenge_config.TARGETS_ENV] = (
                "MIPStarRE.ComparatorDefinitionFrontierFixture.target"
            )
            env.pop(challenge_config.DEFINITIONS_ENV, None)
            if definition_names is not None:
                env[challenge_config.DEFINITIONS_ENV] = definition_names
            return subprocess.run(
                ["lake", "env", "lean", str(extractor)],
                cwd=REPO_ROOT,
                env=env,
                check=False,
                text=True,
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _declaration_names(output: str) -> set[str]:
        return {
            line.split("\t", 1)[0]
            for line in output.splitlines()
            if len(line.split("\t")) in (4, 5)
        }

    def test_real_extraction_stops_only_the_registered_value(self) -> None:
        prefix = "MIPStarRE.ComparatorDefinitionFrontierFixture."
        selected = prefix + "registered"
        result = self._run_extractor(selected)

        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
        names = self._declaration_names(result.stdout)
        self.assertIn(selected, names)
        self.assertIn(prefix + "typeDependency", names)
        self.assertNotIn(prefix + "registeredValueHelper", names)
        self.assertIn(prefix + "ordinary", names)
        self.assertIn(prefix + "ordinaryValueHelper", names)
        self.assertIn(prefix + "ordinaryProofHelper", names)
        selected_row = next(
            line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith(selected + "\t")
        )
        self.assertTrue(selected_row.endswith("\tDEF_SAFE"), selected_row)

        ordinary = self._run_extractor(None)
        self.assertEqual(ordinary.returncode, 0, ordinary.stdout)
        self.assertIn(prefix + "registeredValueHelper", self._declaration_names(ordinary.stdout))

    def test_real_extraction_rejects_bad_registered_names(self) -> None:
        prefix = "MIPStarRE.ComparatorDefinitionFrontierFixture."
        for name, message in (
            (prefix + "missing", "registered definition not found"),
            (prefix + "target", "registered definition is not a definition"),
        ):
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                result = self._run_extractor(name)
                self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
                self.assertIn(message, result.stdout)

            "LDT closure change must follow the explicit baseline-update process "
            "in scripts/comparator/README.md",

            "python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root .\n",

                "python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py "
                f"--root . --challenge {name}",
                workflow,
            )

        for module in (
            "MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar.PauliCompleteness",
            "MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar.LowDegreeSoundness",
            "MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar.PauliSoundness",

        for target in qpbt.targets:

        qpbt = challenge_config.load_challenges(["qpbt"])[0]
        self.assertTrue(
            qpbt.split,
            "the QPBT challenge must mirror the library module partition: a "
            "single module cannot reproduce Lean's per-module auxiliary names",

        allowed_prefixes = ("import Mathlib", "import Challenge")
        for part in [expected / "Challenge.lean", *parts]:
            with self.subTest(module=part.name):
                imports = []
                for line in part.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                    # imports are only legal in the leading block of a module
                    if line.startswith("import "):
                        imports.append(line)
                    elif line.strip():
                        break
                self.assertTrue(imports, f"{part} has no imports")
                for line in imports:
                    self.assertTrue(
                        line.startswith(allowed_prefixes),
                        f"{part}: challenge modules may only import Mathlib and "
                        f"other challenge modules, found {line!r}",

        self.assertEqual(
            palomar.definition_names,
            ("MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedFieldModel",),
        )

        self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), PALOMAR_BASELINE_SHA256)
        text = data.decode("utf-8")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(text.splitlines()), 1000)
        self.assertLessEqual(len(data), 102400)
        self.assertIn("public import Mathlib", text)
        imports = re.findall(r"^(?:public )?import\s+(.+)$", text, re.MULTILINE)
        self.assertEqual(imports, ["Mathlib"])
        self.assertEqual(
            len(re.findall(r"^\s+sorry$", text, re.MULTILINE)),
            5,
        )
        self.assertNotRegex(text, r"^\s*axiom\s", "challenge declares an axiom")
        self.assertEqual(
            len(re.findall(r"^noncomputable def fixedFieldModel\b", text, re.MULTILINE)),
            1,

        for target in palomar.targets:
            self.assertEqual(
                len(re.findall(
                    rf"^theorem {re.escape(target.rsplit('.', 1)[1])}\b",
                    text,
                    re.MULTILINE,
                )),
                1,
            )

        extractor = EXTRACTOR.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn(challenge_config.TARGETS_ENV, extractor)

    55	def source_range_with_context(
    56	    lines: list[str], start: int, end: int
    57	) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    58	    """Extend a declaration range to include adjacent scoped context commands."""
    59	    # Lean's source range starts at a declaration's docstring and can omit a
    60	    # declaration-scoped command immediately before it.  Preserve that command:
    61	    # dropping `open scoped Classical in`, for example, removes the local
    62	    # decidability instances needed to re-elaborate the definition body.
    63	    if start > 1 and re.fullmatch(r"open\s+scoped\s+.+\s+in", lines[start - 2].strip()):

   283	class SplitAssembler(Assembler):
   284	    """Emit one Mathlib-only challenge module per contributing library module.
   285	
   286	    Lean caches an abstracted nested proof and a `match` auxiliary *per module*,
   287	    keyed by the statement and named after the first declaration of that module
   288	    that needs it, and a module only sees the instances its imports declare.  A
   289	    single-file challenge therefore cannot reproduce either name when a library
   290	    fact is needed in two library modules, and it makes every instance visible
